description: We’re Artemis to Ares, a team fascinated by the equipment humans have left behind on the Moon and Mars. Our project, “ The Silent Explorers ”, tells the stories of landers, rovers and stations from The Lunar Modules  to Ingenuity: how they worked, what they discovered, and how they ended. We’re building a research-based, visual website. We’re looking for people with skills in web design, writing, illustration, or space science, and anyone curious about space history.
summary: The Silent Explorers is an interactive storytelling website about spacecraft and equipment left on the Moon and Mars after their missions ended. Through mission stories, a simplified landing-site map, curated NASA catalog records, archival photographs, and a short knowledge check, it explains what these explorers were designed to do, what they discovered, and what remains. The project turns space-mission information into an approachable experience for students and curious visitors. It highlights the lasting scientific value of lunar and Martian exploration while distinguishing planned hardware left behind from equipment lost unexpectedly. Links to NASA records and image sources help visitors explore the underlying information.
details:
The Silent Explorers is an educational, interactive story about NASA spacecraft and equipment left on the Moon and Mars after their missions. Visitors can read a scroll-led story, explore 11 mission chapters and equipment guides, view a simplified landing-site map, browse NASA archive photographs, and take a short quiz.

The project also includes a curated index of 15 NSSDCA catalog records—7 Moon and 8 Mars records. Their linked NASA identifiers support the destination counts, filters, distribution bars, and CSV export. This is a selected subset, not a download of the full catalog; categories and mission-end notes are project summaries.

The site is built with React, TypeScript, CSS, Vite, and Lucide icons. It uses NASA Image and Video Library search results when available, alongside locally bundled archive images. The map is an educational coordinate plot, not a navigation tool. The project aims to connect the engineering and science of each mission with what remains after it ends.
